description:
Tier 2, lower value than argon2id because bcrypt is CPU-bound with a 4 KB state, not memory-hard, and bcrypt_elixir's dirty-scheduler cost is small per hash; still common (Phoenix defaults), and the same yield and kill-cleanup story applies. Blowfish key schedule with the EksBlowfishSetup cost loop (2^cost iterations), the four 256-entry S-boxes and the P-array as module attributes (4 KB of constants: the first real test of defk-ivt with large binary attributes), and the 64-byte Base64 variant bcrypt uses for its output string (Elixir side).

Vectors: the OpenBSD test vectors and bcrypt_elixir's outputs. Expected verdict: marginal (parity with reference C), with the runtime-contract measurements beside.

Needs: defk-w38, defk-ivt (large binary attributes), defk-n4r.4, the builtins ticket (rotates not needed; u32 masked arithmetic is). Blocked by the argon2id ticket to reuse its harness and governance text.

Done when: vectors pass, agreement with bcrypt_elixir holds for cost 4-12, verdict recorded.
title: bcrypt from scratch vs bcrypt_elixir (after argon2id)
